        let mut file = fs::File::create(&tmp_path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        file.write_all(content.as_bytes())
            .map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        file.sync_all().map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        fs::rename(&tmp_path, &file_path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;

        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn load(id: &str) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
        let dir = Self::sessions_dir()?;
        let file_path = dir.join(format!("{id}.json"));
        Self::load_from(&file_path)
    }

    fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
        if !path.exists() {
            return Err(SessionError::NotFound(path.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
        }
        let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        serde_json::from_str(&content).map_err(SessionError::Parse)
    }
}

fn days_to_ymd(mut days: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    days += 719_468;
    let era = if days >= 0 { days } else { days - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (days - era * 146_097) as u32;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    (year, m, d)
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum SessionError {
    Io(std::io::Error),
    Serialize(serde_json::Error),
    Parse(serde_json::Error),
    NotFound(String),
    NoHomeDir,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for SessionError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Io(e) => write!(f, "session I/O error: {e}"),
            Self::Serialize(e) => write!(f, "session serialize error: {e}"),
            Self::Parse(e) => write!(f, "session parse error: {e}"),
            Self::NotFound(path) => write!(f, "session not found: {path}"),
            Self::NoHomeDir => write!(f, "could not determine home directory"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for SessionError {}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::services::git_analysis::{ChangedFile, FileStatus};

    fn make_test_analysis() -> GitAnalysis {
        GitAnalysis {
            repo_path: "/tmp/test-repo".to_string(),
            current_branch: "feature-branch".to_string(),
            default_branch: "main".to_string(),
            merge_base: "abc123def456".to_string(),
            diff: "diff --git a/file.rs b/file.rs\n+new line".to_string(),
            changed_files: vec![ChangedFile {
                path: "file.rs".to_string(),
                status: FileStatus::Modified,
            }],
            commit_count: 3,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_new_session_generates_id() {
        let session = ReviewSession::new(make_test_analysis());
        assert!(session.id.starts_with("review-"));
        assert_eq!(session.branch, "feature-branch");
        assert_eq!(session.default_branch, "main");
        assert!(!session.created_at.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_save_and_load_roundtrip() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("sherpa_test_sessions_roundtrip");
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();

        let session = ReviewSession::new(make_test_analysis());
        let file_path = dir.join(format!("{}.json", session.id));

        let content = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&session).unwrap();
        fs::write(&file_path, content).unwrap();

        let loaded = ReviewSession::load_from(&file_path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(loaded.id, session.id);
        assert_eq!(loaded.repo_path, session.repo_path);
        assert_eq!(loaded.branch, session.branch);
        assert_eq!(loaded.changed_files.len(), 1);

        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_load_nonexistent_returns_error() {
        let path = PathBuf::from("/tmp/sherpa_nonexistent_session/does-not-exist.json");
        let result = ReviewSession::load_from(&path);
        assert!(result.is_err());
        let err = result.unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, SessionError::NotFound(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_created_at_is_iso8601() {
        let session = ReviewSession::new(make_test_analysis());
        assert!(session.created_at.ends_with('Z'));
        assert!(session.created_at.contains('T'));
    }
}

async fn generate_section(
    session_id: &str,
    section: &str,
    instruction: &str,
    get_cached: fn(&ReviewSession) -> &Option<String>,
    set_cached: fn(&mut ReviewSession, String),
) -> std::result::Result<(String, bool), String> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(session_id)
        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to load session: {e}"))?;

    if let Some(cached) = get_cached(&session) {
        return Ok((cached.clone(), true));
    }

    let cli = load_selected_cli().ok_or("No AI backend configured")?;
    let context = build_ai_context(&session);
    let prompt = AiPrompt {
        context,
        instruction: instruction.to_string(),
    };

    let content = ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(session_id)
        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to reload session: {e}"))?;
    set_cached(&mut session, content.clone());
    let _ = session.save();

    Ok((content, false))
}

pub struct ChatForm {
    message: String,
}

#[debug_handler]
async fn summary_chat(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
    Form(form): Form<ChatForm>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    let user_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "user".to_string(),
        content: form.message.clone(),
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(user_msg);

    let cli = load_selected_cli();
    let ai_response = if let Some(cli) = cli {
        let context = build_ai_context(&session);
        let prompt = AiPrompt {
            context,
            instruction: format!(
                "The user asks: {}\n\nRespond helpfully based on the code changes above.",
                form.message
            ),
        };
        match ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt).await {
            Ok(response) => response,
            Err(e) => format!("AI error: {e}"),
        }
    } else {
        "No AI backend configured. Please set up an AI backend first.".to_string()
    };

    let ai_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "assistant".to_string(),
        content: ai_response,
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(ai_msg);
    let _ = session.save();

    let last_two: Vec<_> = session.chat_messages[session.chat_messages.len() - 2..].to_vec();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/_chat_messages.html",
        data!({"messages": last_two}),
    )
}

fn chrono_now() -> String {
    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
        .as_millis();
    let secs = millis / 1000;
    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
    format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}")
}

pub fn page_routes() -> Routes {
    Routes::new()
        .prefix("/review")
        .add("/:session_id/summary", get(summary_page))
        .add("/:session_id/summary/overview", get(summary_overview))
        .add("/:session_id/summary/changes", get(summary_changes))
        .add("/:session_id/summary/approach", get(summary_approach))
        .add("/:session_id/summary/skip/:section", get(section_skip))
        .add("/:session_id/summary/chat", post(summary_chat))
}

pub fn api_routes() -> Routes {
    Routes::new().prefix("/api/review")
}

use serial_test::serial;
use sherpa::app::App;
use sherpa::services::git_analysis::{ChangedFile, FileStatus, GitAnalysis};
use sherpa::services::review_session::ReviewSession;

fn create_test_session() -> ReviewSession {
    let analysis = GitAnalysis {
        repo_path: "/tmp/test-repo".to_string(),
        current_branch: "feature-test".to_string(),
        default_branch: "main".to_string(),
        merge_base: "abc123".to_string(),
        diff: "diff --git a/file.rs b/file.rs\n--- a/file.rs\n+++ b/file.rs\n+new line\n+another\n-removed"
            .to_string(),
        changed_files: vec![
            ChangedFile {
                path: "src/lib.rs".to_string(),
                status: FileStatus::Modified,
            },
            ChangedFile {
                path: "src/new.rs".to_string(),
                status: FileStatus::Added,
            },
        ],
        commit_count: 5,
    };
    let session = ReviewSession::new(analysis);
    session.save().expect("save test session");
    session
}

fn cleanup_session(id: &str) {
    if let Ok(dir) = ReviewSession::sessions_dir() {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(dir.join(format!("{id}.json")));
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
#[serial]
async fn can_get_summary_page() {
    let session = create_test_session();
    let session_id = session.id.clone();

    request::<App, _, _>(|request, _ctx| async move {
        let res = request
            .get(&format!("/review/{session_id}/summary"))
            .await;

        assert_eq!(res.status_code(), 200);

        let body = res.text();
        assert!(body.contains("Review Summary"), "page should contain heading");
        assert!(body.contains("feature-test"), "page should show branch name");
        assert!(body.contains("Metrics"), "page should contain metrics section");
        assert!(
            body.contains("hx-get"),
            "page should have HTMX triggers for AI sections"
        );
        assert!(body.contains("Chat"), "page should contain chat section");

        cleanup_session(&session_id);
    })
    .await;
}

}

use axum::Form;
use loco_rs::prelude::*;

    ai_cli::{self, AiPrompt},

    config::SherpaConfig,
    review_session::{ChatMessage, ReviewSession},
};

fn load_selected_cli() -> Option<AiCli> {
    SherpaConfig::default_path()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|p| SherpaConfig::load(&p).ok())
        .and_then(|c| c.ai.selected_cli)
}

fn build_changed_files_summary(session: &ReviewSession) -> String {
    session
        .changed_files
        .iter()
        .map(|f| format!("{}\t{}", f.status, f.path))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\n")
}

fn build_ai_context(session: &ReviewSession) -> String {
    let files_summary = build_changed_files_summary(session);
    ai_cli::build_context(
        &session.branch,
        &session.default_branch,
        &files_summary,
        &session.diff,
    )
}

#[debug_handler]
async fn summary_page(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/summary.html",
        data!({
            "session_id": session.id,
            "branch": session.branch,
            "default_branch": session.default_branch,
            "metrics": session.metrics,
            "chat_messages": session.chat_messages,
        }),
    )
}

## 1. AI CLI Invocation

Both CLIs support non-interactive mode:

```rust
// Claude Code:
// claude -p --print "your prompt here"
// Reads from args, prints to stdout, exits.

// OpenCode:
// opencode run "your prompt here"
// Same pattern: prints result, exits.
```

Use `tokio::process::Command` — you're already in an async Loco context and it avoids blocking the Tokio runtime (unlike `spawn_blocking` + `std::process::Command`, which is fine but less idiomatic for streaming later).

**Concrete service** (`src/services/ai_cli.rs`):

```rust
use tokio::process::Command;
use crate::services::cli_detection::AiCli;

pub struct AiPrompt {
    pub system_context: String, // diff, branch info, file list
    pub instruction: String,    // section-specific ask
}

pub async fn generate(cli: AiCli, prompt: &AiPrompt) -> Result<String, AiCliError> {
    let full_prompt = format!("{}\n\n{}", prompt.system_context, prompt.instruction);
    
    let output = match cli {
        AiCli::Claude => {
            Command::new("claude")
                .args(["--print", &full_prompt])
                .output()
                .await?
        }
        AiCli::Opencode => {
            Command::new("opencode")
                .args(["run", &full_prompt])
                .output()
                .await?
        }
    };
    
    if !output.status.success() {
        return Err(AiCliError::CliFailure(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string()));
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
}
```

**Prompt structure** — build a shared context block once, vary only the instruction:

```
Context: You're reviewing a code change on branch `{branch}` against `{default_branch}`.
Changed files: {file_list_with_statuses}
Diff: {diff (truncated to ~8k chars if needed)}
```

| Section | Instruction |
|---------|------------|
| Project Overview | "Based on the repository structure and changed files, write a 2-3 sentence summary of what this project is and which area these changes affect. Be concise." |
| Change Summary | "Summarize what changed in this branch in 3-5 bullet points. Focus on what was added, modified, or removed. Be specific about file names." |
| Implementation Approach | "Describe the implementation approach taken in these changes in 2-3 sentences. Note any design patterns, architectural decisions, or potential concerns." |

**Watch out for:**
- **Diff size**: `claude --print` and `opencode run` pass prompts as CLI args. Very large diffs may hit ARG_MAX. If `diff.len() > 100_000`, truncate to the `--name-status` summary + first N hunks. Alternatively, pipe via stdin (claude supports `-p` with stdin piping).
- **Timeout**: Set a timeout (~60s). `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(60), generate(...))`.
- **Working directory**: Run the CLI in a temp dir or the repo dir — avoid leaking Sherpa's own directory context to the AI.

**Go with Option A/C hybrid** — they're effectively the same thing. Use `hx-trigger="load"` on each section placeholder:

**Why this approach:**
- All 3 AI requests fire in parallel from the browser — no serialization
- Each section is independently loadable, retriable, skippable
- Metrics section renders immediately (no AI needed)
- No JS required — pure HTMX

## 4. AI Section Caching

**Yes, cache in ReviewSession.** Add optional fields:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReviewSession {
    // ... existing fields ...
    
    #[serde(default)]
    pub summary: SummaryData,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct SummaryData {
    pub overview: Option<String>,
    pub changes: Option<String>,
    pub approach: Option<String>,
}
```

The `#[serde(default)]` on `summary` ensures backward compatibility with existing session JSON files that lack this field.

**Loading flow in each section endpoint:**

```rust
async fn summary_overview(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| /* ... */)?;
    
    // Cache hit → return immediately
    if let Some(ref content) = session.summary.overview {
        return format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_content.html", 
            data!({"title": "Project Overview", "content": content}));
    }
    
    // Cache miss → invoke AI
    let config = load_config();
    let cli = config.ai.selected_cli.ok_or(/* ... */)?;
    let prompt = build_overview_prompt(&session);
    
    match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(60), ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt)).await {
        Ok(Ok(content)) => {
            session.summary.overview = Some(content.clone());
            let _ = session.save(); // best-effort persist
            format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_content.html",
                data!({"title": "Project Overview", "content": content}))
        }
        Ok(Err(e)) => {
            format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_error.html",
                data!({"title": "Project Overview", "error": e.to_string(), 
                       "retry_url": format!("/review/{}/summary/overview", session_id)}))
        }
        Err(_) => {
            format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_error.html",
                data!({"title": "Project Overview", "error": "AI request timed out",
                       "retry_url": format!("/review/{}/summary/overview", session_id)}))
        }
    }
}
```

**Page reload = instant** since all cached sections return immediately. Uncached ones re-trigger AI.

## 1. AI CLI Invocation

Both CLIs support non-interactive mode:

```rust
// Claude Code:
// claude -p --print "your prompt here"
// Reads from args, prints to stdout, exits.

// OpenCode:
// opencode run "your prompt here"
// Same pattern: prints result, exits.
```

Use `tokio::process::Command` — you're already in an async Loco context and it avoids blocking the Tokio runtime (unlike `spawn_blocking` + `std::process::Command`, which is fine but less idiomatic for streaming later).

**Concrete service** (`src/services/ai_cli.rs`):

```rust
use tokio::process::Command;
use crate::services::cli_detection::AiCli;

pub struct AiPrompt {
    pub system_context: String, // diff, branch info, file list
    pub instruction: String,    // section-specific ask
}

pub async fn generate(cli: AiCli, prompt: &AiPrompt) -> Result<String, AiCliError> {
    let full_prompt = format!("{}\n\n{}", prompt.system_context, prompt.instruction);
    
    let output = match cli {
        AiCli::Claude => {
            Command::new("claude")
                .args(["--print", &full_prompt])
                .output()
                .await?
        }
        AiCli::Opencode => {
            Command::new("opencode")
                .args(["run", &full_prompt])
                .output()
                .await?
        }
    };
    
    if !output.status.success() {
        return Err(AiCliError::CliFailure(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string()));
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
}
```

**Prompt structure** — build a shared context block once, vary only the instruction:

```
Context: You're reviewing a code change on branch `{branch}` against `{default_branch}`.
Changed files: {file_list_with_statuses}
Diff: {diff (truncated to ~8k chars if needed)}
```

| Section | Instruction |
|---------|------------|
| Project Overview | "Based on the repository structure and changed files, write a 2-3 sentence summary of what this project is and which area these changes affect. Be concise." |
| Change Summary | "Summarize what changed in this branch in 3-5 bullet points. Focus on what was added, modified, or removed. Be specific about file names." |
| Implementation Approach | "Describe the implementation approach taken in these changes in 2-3 sentences. Note any design patterns, architectural decisions, or potential concerns." |

**Watch out for:**
- **Diff size**: `claude --print` and `opencode run` pass prompts as CLI args. Very large diffs may hit ARG_MAX. If `diff.len() > 100_000`, truncate to the `--name-status` summary + first N hunks. Alternatively, pipe via stdin (claude supports `-p` with stdin piping).
- **Timeout**: Set a timeout (~60s). `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(60), generate(...))`.
- **Working directory**: Run the CLI in a temp dir or the repo dir — avoid leaking Sherpa's own directory context to the AI.

**Loading flow in each section endpoint:**

```rust
async fn summary_overview(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| /* ... */)?;
    
    // Cache hit → return immediately
    if let Some(ref content) = session.summary.overview {
        return format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_content.html", 
            data!({"title": "Project Overview", "content": content}));
    }
    
    // Cache miss → invoke AI
    let config = load_config();
    let cli = config.ai.selected_cli.ok_or(/* ... */)?;
    let prompt = build_overview_prompt(&session);
    
    match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(60), ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt)).await {
        Ok(Ok(content)) => {
            session.summary.overview = Some(content.clone());
            let _ = session.save(); // best-effort persist
            format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_content.html",
                data!({"title": "Project Overview", "content": content}))
        }
        Ok(Err(e)) => {
            format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_error.html",
                data!({"title": "Project Overview", "error": e.to_string(), 
                       "retry_url": format!("/review/{}/summary/overview", session_id)}))
        }
        Err(_) => {
            format::render().view(&v, "review/_section_error.html",
                data!({"title": "Project Overview", "error": "AI request timed out",
                       "retry_url": format!("/review/{}/summary/overview", session_id)}))
        }
    }
}
```

# Sherpa — AI-Guided Code Review Tool

Sherpa pairs a developer reviewing code changes (branch diffs) with an AI guide. Point it at a local Git repository, and the tool analyzes the current branch's changes against its merge base, providing a step-by-step guided review powered by AI.

**Stack:** [Loco.rs](https://loco.rs) (Rust backend), HTMX + FlyonUI (UI), diff2html (client-side diff rendering).

## Prerequisites

- [devbox](https://devbox.jdx.dev/) — development environment manager
- [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) stable toolchain (managed via devbox)

## Getting Started

```sh
# Install development tools
devbox install

# Start the development server
cargo loco start
```

The app starts on **http://localhost:5150**.

### Useful Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `GET /api` | Home (JSON) |
| `GET /_health` | Health check |
| `GET /_ping` | Ping |

## Development

```sh
# Run all quality gates
devbox run qa

# Individual commands
devbox run check    # cargo check
devbox run test     # cargo test
devbox run lint     # cargo clippy
devbox run fmt      # cargo fmt
devbox run dev      # cargo loco start
```

## Project Structure

```
├── assets/
│   ├── i18n/           # Internationalization files
│   ├── static/         # Static assets (CSS, JS, images)
│   └── views/          # Tera HTML templates
├── config/
│   ├── development.yaml
│   ├── test.yaml
│   └── production.yaml
├── src/
│   ├── app.rs          # Application hooks and router
│   ├── bin/main.rs     # CLI entry point
│   ├── controllers/    # Request handlers
│   ├── initializers/   # View engine setup
│   └── views/          # Response structs
└── tests/
    └── requests/       # Integration tests
```

00001| # PRD: Sherpa — AI-Guided Code Review Tool
00002| 
00003| ## Overview
00004| Sherpa is a single-user local tool that pairs a developer reviewing code changes (branch diffs) with an AI guide. The developer points Sherpa at a local Git repository, and the tool analyzes the current branch's changes against its merge base. An AI (via `opencode` or `claude` CLI, user's choice) then provides a project summary, change analysis, and a step-by-step guided review — grouping changes in whatever way makes the review easiest to understand. The developer walks through each step, chatting with the AI, and validates changes as they go. Review progress is persisted to disk so sessions can be resumed.
00005| 
00006| The stack is Loco.rs (Rust backend), HTMX + FlyonUI (UI), diff2html (client-side diff rendering), and devbox for dev environment management.
00007| 
00008| ## Goals
00009| - Provide AI-guided, step-by-step code review that makes complex changesets easy to understand
00010| - Auto-detect the branch merge base and analyze all changes on the current branch
00011| - Let the AI fully drive how changes are grouped and ordered for review
00012| - Persist review state (validated steps, chat history) so reviews can be resumed
00013| - Support both `opencode` and `claude` CLI as AI backends, user-selectable from the UI
00014| - Deliver a smooth HTMX-driven UI with FlyonUI components and diff2html for diffs
00015| 
00016| ## Quality Gates
00017| 
00018| These commands must pass for every user story:
00019| - `cargo check` — Compilation check
00020| - `cargo test` — Test suite
00021| - `cargo clippy` — Lint check
00022| 
00023| For UI stories, also include:
00024| - Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
00025| 
00026| ## User Stories
00027| 
00028| ### US-001: Initialize project scaffolding with Loco.rs and devbox
00029| As a developer, I want the project bootstrapped with Loco.rs, devbox configuration, and basic dependencies so that I have a working foundation to build on.
00030| 
00031| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00032| - [ ] Loco.rs project initialized with `loco` CLI (SaaS or lightweight template — whichever fits single-user local tool best)
00033| - [ ] `devbox.toml` (or `.devbox.toml`) configures Rust toolchain, `cargo`, and any needed tools
00034| - [ ] `cargo check` passes on the scaffolded project
00035| - [ ] A `README.md` documents how to `devbox install && cargo run` to start the app
00036| - [ ] The app starts and responds on `localhost` with a basic health check endpoint
00037| 
00038| ### US-002: Serve HTMX + FlyonUI frontend from Loco
00039| As a developer, I want Loco to serve HTML pages using HTMX and FlyonUI so that the UI is rendered server-side with dynamic updates.
00040| 
00041| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00042| - [ ] Loco serves static assets (JS, CSS) including HTMX, FlyonUI CSS/JS, and diff2html
00043| - [ ] A Tera (or similar) template engine is configured for server-side HTML rendering
00044| - [ ] A base layout template includes HTMX script, FlyonUI styles, and diff2html assets
00045| - [ ] A test page renders at `/` using the base layout with a FlyonUI component visible
00046| - [ ] HTMX `hx-get` works on the test page (e.g., a button that loads a fragment)
00047| 
00048| ### US-003: AI CLI detection and user selection
00049| As a user, I want to choose between `opencode` and `claude` CLI as my AI backend so that I can use whichever tool I have installed.
00050| 
00051| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00052| - [ ] On startup, the backend detects which CLI tools are available (`which opencode`, `which claude`)
00053| - [ ] The UI presents a selection screen showing available CLIs (grayed out if not found)
00054| - [ ] The user's choice is stored in a config file (e.g., `~/.sherpa/config.toml` or project-local `.sherpa/config.toml`)
00055| - [ ] If only one CLI is available, it is pre-selected but the user can still confirm
00056| - [ ] The selected CLI is used for all subsequent AI interactions in the session
00057| - [ ] If neither CLI is found, an error message explains what to install
00058| 
00059| ### US-004: Repository path input and Git analysis
00060| As a user, I want to provide a directory path so that Sherpa can analyze the Git branch history of that repository.
00061| 
00062| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00063| - [ ] The UI shows a text input for the directory path (with a "Browse" affordance or paste support)
00064| - [ ] The backend validates: directory exists, is a Git repo, has a checked-out branch
00065| - [ ] The backend auto-detects the merge base of the current branch against the default branch (`main`, `master`, or configured default)
00066| - [ ] If the current branch IS the default branch, show an error: "You're on the default branch — switch to a feature branch"
00067| - [ ] On success, the backend extracts the full diff (`git diff <merge-base>..HEAD`) and the list of changed files
00068| - [ ] The diff data and file list are stored in memory (or temp storage) for subsequent analysis
00069| - [ ] Loading indicator shown while Git analysis runs
00070| 
00071| ### US-005: AI-generated project and change summary screen
00072| As a user, I want to see an AI-generated overview of the project, the branch changes, implementation approach, and basic metrics so that I understand the context before reviewing.
00073| 
00074| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00075| - [ ] The summary screen displays four sections: Project Overview, Change Summary, Implementation Approach, and Metrics
00076| - [ ] "Project Overview" is generated by the AI analyzing the repo (e.g., README, directory structure, key files)
00077| - [ ] "Change Summary" is generated by the AI analyzing the diff — explains WHAT the changes introduce
00078| - [ ] "Implementation Approach" is generated by the AI — explains HOW the changes are implemented
00079| - [ ] "Metrics" section shows: number of files changed, lines added, lines removed, number of commits on the branch
00080| - [ ] Each AI section shows a loading state while the AI CLI processes
00081| - [ ] If an AI call fails, the section shows an error with "Retry" and "Skip" buttons
00082| - [ ] A chat input is available at the bottom of the summary screen for the user to ask questions about the changes
00083| - [ ] A "Start Review" button is visible to proceed to the guided review
00084| 
00085| ### US-006: AI-driven change grouping for guided review
00086| As a user, I want the AI to group the branch changes into logical review steps so that I can review them in the most understandable order.
00087| 
00088| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00089| - [ ] After the user clicks "Start Review", the AI is prompted to analyze the full diff and produce a review plan
00090| - [ ] The review plan is a list of steps, each with: a title, a list of file/hunk references, and a brief rationale for the grouping
00091| - [ ] The AI may group by feature, concept, layer, or any strategy it deems best — it is NOT constrained to file-by-file or commit-by-commit
00092| - [ ] A single file's changes may be split across multiple steps if the AI determines it aids understanding
00093| - [ ] The review plan is displayed as a sidebar/progress indicator showing all steps
00094| - [ ] Loading indicator shown while the AI generates the plan
00095| - [ ] If the AI call fails, show error with "Retry" and "Skip" (skip falls back to file-by-file grouping)
00096| - [ ] The review plan is persisted to disk as part of the review state
00097| 
00098| ### US-007: Step-by-step review UI with diff and AI explanation
00099| As a user, I want each review step to show the diff, an AI explanation, and contextual information so that I can understand each change thoroughly.
00100| 
00101| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00102| - [ ] Each step shows: the diff for the grouped changes rendered with diff2html (unified view by default)
00103| - [ ] An AI-generated explanation of the changes in this step is displayed above or beside the diff
00104| - [ ] If there is a previous step, an AI-generated explanation of how this step relates to the previous one is shown
00105| - [ ] For each changed symbol (module, class, function), its name is displayed with an AI-generated description of its responsibilities
00106| - [ ] diff2html renders with syntax highlighting appropriate to the file type
00107| - [ ] The step title and step number (e.g., "Step 3 of 8") are visible
00108| - [ ] The sidebar/progress indicator highlights the current step
00109| - [ ] If any AI call for the step fails, the section shows an error with "Retry" and "Skip" options
00110| 
00111| ### US-008: Chat interface with step-scoped highlighting
00112| As a user, I want a chat input on each review step to discuss changes with the AI, with full history visible but current-step messages highlighted.
00113| 
00114| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00115| - [ ] A chat panel is visible on each review step
00116| - [ ] The user can type a message and receive an AI response (via the selected CLI)
00117| - [ ] The AI receives context: the current step's diff, explanation, and the overall review plan
00118| - [ ] Full chat history from all steps is available and scrollable
00119| - [ ] Messages from the current step are visually highlighted (e.g., different background color or a divider)
00120| - [ ] Messages from previous steps are dimmed or visually differentiated
00121| - [ ] Chat messages are persisted as part of the review state
00122| - [ ] The chat auto-scrolls to the latest message
00123| 
00124| ### US-009: Step validation and navigation
00125| As a user, I want to validate each review step and navigate between steps so that I can mark changes as reviewed and move through the review.
00126| 
00127| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00128| - [ ] A "Validate & Next" button marks the current step as reviewed and advances to the next step
00129| - [ ] A "Previous" button navigates to the prior step (without un-validating it)
00130| - [ ] Clicking a step in the sidebar navigates directly to that step
00131| - [ ] Validated steps show a checkmark in the sidebar
00132| - [ ] The user can re-visit validated steps and see the diff/explanation/chat again
00133| - [ ] Validation state is persisted to disk
00134| 
00135| ### US-010: Review completion summary screen
00136| As a user, I want to see the summary screen again when all steps are validated, with a list of reviewed changes, so that I have a final overview.
00137| 
00138| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00139| - [ ] When the last step is validated, the user is redirected to the summary screen
00140| - [ ] The summary screen now includes a "Reviewed Changes" section listing all review steps
00141| - [ ] Each reviewed step is shown as a collapsible/foldable card — folded by default
00142| - [ ] Unfolding a card shows: step title, files involved, the AI explanation, and the chat messages from that step
00143| - [ ] The original summary sections (Project Overview, Change Summary, Implementation, Metrics) are still visible
00144| - [ ] The chat input is still available for final questions
00145| - [ ] A visual indicator (e.g., banner) confirms "Review Complete — all changes reviewed"
00146| 
00147| ### US-011: Review state persistence and resume
00148| As a user, I want my review progress saved to disk so that I can close the tool and resume later where I left off.
00149| 
00150| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00151| - [ ] Review state is saved to a `.sherpa/` directory inside the analyzed repository (or a configurable location)
00152| - [ ] State includes: repository path, branch name, merge base commit, review plan, validation status per step, and full chat history
00153| - [ ] On startup, if a saved review exists for the current repo+branch, the user is prompted: "Resume previous review?" or "Start fresh?"
00154| - [ ] Resuming restores the user to the last un-validated step with all previous state intact
00155| - [ ] If the branch has new commits since the saved review, warn the user: "Branch has changed since last review — resume may be outdated"
00156| - [ ] State is saved automatically after each step validation and chat message (no manual save)
00157| 
00158| ### US-012: Error handling for AI CLI calls
00159| As a user, I want clear error messages and recovery options when AI CLI calls fail so that a single failure doesn't block my entire review.
00160| 
00161| **Acceptance Criteria:**
00162| - [ ] All AI CLI calls have a configurable timeout (default: 120 seconds)
00163| - [ ] On failure (timeout, non-zero exit, malformed output), the UI shows the error message inline
00164| - [ ] Each failed section offers "Retry" (re-run the same call) and "Skip" (proceed without that AI output)
00165| - [ ] Skipped sections show a placeholder: "AI analysis skipped — click to retry"
00166| - [ ] Errors are logged to `.sherpa/logs/` for debugging
00167| - [ ] Network/CLI errors do NOT crash the application or lose review state
00168| 
00169| ## Functional Requirements
00170| - FR-1: The backend must shell out to `opencode` or `claude` CLI to perform AI analysis, passing prompts via stdin or arguments and capturing stdout
00171| - FR-2: The backend must use `git` CLI commands to extract diff, log, merge-base, and file information
00172| - FR-3: The UI must be server-rendered with Tera templates, using HTMX for dynamic updates without full page reloads
00173| - FR-4: FlyonUI components must be used for all UI elements (buttons, cards, inputs, navigation, modals)
00174| - FR-5: diff2html must be loaded client-side to render diffs from unified diff format provided by the backend
00175| - FR-6: All AI-generated content must be streamed or loaded asynchronously with visible loading indicators
00176| - FR-7: The review state must be serializable to JSON (or TOML) and written to disk atomically (write-tmp-then-rename)
00177| - FR-8: The chat interface must send user messages via HTMX POST and append AI responses via HTMX swap
00178| - FR-9: The guided review sidebar must update step status via HTMX without full page reload
00179| - FR-10: The application must work fully offline (no external services beyond the locally installed AI CLI)
00180| 
00181| ## Non-Goals (Out of Scope)
00182| - Multi-user support or authentication
00183| - Remote repository analysis (only local repos)
00184| - Direct code modification or PR creation from within the tool (review only for v1)
00185| - Custom AI model configuration (model selection is delegated to the CLI tool)
00186| - Support for non-Git version control systems
00187| - Side-by-side diff view (unified only for v1 — side-by-side can come later)
00188| - Branch selection UI (always uses current checked-out branch)
00189| - Integration with GitHub/GitLab APIs for PR metadata
00190| 
00191| ## Technical Considerations
00192| - **Loco.rs** provides the HTTP server, routing, and middleware. Use its controller/view pattern for serving templates.
00193| - **Tera templates** for server-side HTML rendering — Loco supports this natively or via middleware.
00194| - **HTMX** handles all dynamic interactions — form submissions, partial page updates, polling for AI responses.
00195| - **FlyonUI** is a Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI-based component library — ensure the Tailwind build pipeline is configured (possibly via `devbox` task).
00196| - **diff2html** loaded as a client-side JS library. The backend provides raw unified diff strings; diff2html renders them in the browser.
00197| - **AI CLI invocation** should use Rust's `tokio::process::Command` for async subprocess execution with timeout support.
00198| - **State persistence** as JSON files in `.sherpa/` — consider using `serde_json` for serialization.
00199| - **devbox** should configure: Rust toolchain, Node.js (for Tailwind/FlyonUI build), and any other tools.
00200| - **Git operations** via `git2` crate (libgit2 bindings) for merge-base detection and diff extraction, with fallback to `git` CLI if needed.
00201| 
00202| ## Success Metrics
00203| - User can go from `cargo run` to viewing a review summary in under 60 seconds (excluding AI response time)
00204| - All review steps can be validated without errors on a typical feature branch (10-50 changed files)
00205| - Review state persists correctly across application restarts
00206| - AI grouping produces meaningful steps (not just file-by-file) for branches with cross-cutting changes
00207| - Chat responses include relevant context from the current review step
00208| 
00209| ## Open Questions
00210| - Should the tool support reviewing stashed changes or only committed changes on the branch?
00211| - What is the maximum diff size the AI CLI can handle in a single prompt? May need chunking strategy for very large branches.
00212| - Should the `.sherpa/` state directory be gitignored by default (add to the repo's `.gitignore`)?
00213| - Should there be a "reject" action per step (in addition to "validate") for future use when the tool supports requesting changes?
00214| - How should the tool handle binary files in the diff (images, compiled assets)?

## Bottom Line

Keep the data model flat with file-path + line-range references (no pre-parsed hunk indexing). Ask the AI for JSON with a markdown fence wrapper and parse with a lenient extractor. US-006 scope = generate the plan, persist it, and redirect to a new `/review/{id}/guide` page that shows the plan as a list — don't build the step-by-step diff viewer (that's US-007).

### 1. Data Model — Add to `review_session.rs`

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReviewPlan {
    pub steps: Vec<ReviewStep>,
    pub generated_at: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReviewStep {
    pub title: String,
    pub rationale: String,
    pub file_refs: Vec<FileRef>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FileRef {
    pub path: String,
    /// Optional line range within the diff (start_line, end_line) — refers to
    /// lines in the unified diff output for this file, NOT the source file.
    /// None means "entire file's diff."
    pub diff_lines: Option<(usize, usize)>,

```

Add to `ReviewSession`:

```

**Why `diff_lines` over hunk indexes:** The diff is already stored as a string. Line ranges within the per-file diff segment are stable, trivially extractable with a substring split, and don't require a pre-parsing step or separate hunk data structure. In US-007, you split the stored diff by `diff --git` headers, then extract the line range. Hunk indexes would require building an index mapping upfront and keeping it in sync — unnecessary complexity.

### 2. AI Prompt Strategy

Add a `review_plan_instruction()` to `ai_cli.rs`:

```rust
pub fn review_plan_instruction() -> &'static str {
    "Analyze this diff and create a step-by-step review plan. Group changes by \
     feature, concept, or architectural layer — NOT necessarily one step per file. \
     A single file's changes may appear in multiple steps if they serve different purposes.\n\n\
     Respond with ONLY a JSON object inside a ```json fence, no other text:\n\
     ```json\n\
     {\n\
       \"steps\": [\n\
         {\n\
           \"title\": \"Short descriptive title\",\n\
           \"rationale\": \"Why review these changes together\",\n\
           \"file_refs\": [\n\
             {\"path\": \"src/foo.rs\", \"diff_lines\": [10, 45]},\n\
             {\"path\": \"src/bar.rs\", \"diff_lines\": null}\n\
           ]\n\
         }\n\
       ]\n\
     }\n\
     ```\n\
     Use diff_lines to reference specific line ranges within each file's diff section, \
     or null for the entire file. Order steps in recommended review sequence."
}
```

**JSON extraction strategy:** Don't trust the AI to return clean JSON. Write a helper that:
1. Tries `serde_json::from_str` on the raw output
2. Falls back to regex-extracting content between ` ```json ` and ` ``` ` fences
3. Falls back to finding the first `{` to last `}` substring

```rust
pub fn extract_json_from_response(raw: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    // Try whole string
    if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(raw).is_ok() {
        return Ok(raw.to_string());
    }
    // Try fenced block
    if let Some(start) = raw.find("```json") {
        let after = &raw[start + 7..];
        if let Some(end) = after.find("```") {
            return Ok(after[..end].trim().to_string());
        }
    }
    // Try first { to last }
    if let (Some(s), Some(e)) = (raw.find('{'), raw.rfind('}')) {
        return Ok(raw[s..=e].to_string());
    }
    Err("Could not extract JSON from AI response".to_string())
}
```

Then `serde_json::from_str::<ReviewPlanResponse>(&extracted)` with a wrapper struct. This 3-tier approach handles 99% of LLM JSON output variations.

**Option (a): Navigate to `/review/{id}/guide`.** This is the right boundary.

When the user clicks "Start Review":
- `hx-get="/review/{id}/guide/plan"` with `hx-target` replacing the button area with a loading indicator
- Server generates the plan (or returns cached), saves to session, then returns an `HX-Redirect: /review/{id}/guide` header
- The `/review/{id}/guide` page shows the plan as an ordered list (this is the skeleton that US-007 will fill with diff content and US-009 with navigation)

**Why a new page:** The guide page has fundamentally different layout (sidebar + content area) vs. the summary page (linear card stack). Trying to morph one into the other via HTMX swap would be fragile and fight the layout.

**US-006 scope boundary:**

- ✅ Plan persisted to session JSON
- ✅ Redirect to `/review/{id}/guide` which renders the plan as a step list
- ✅ Retry/Skip on plan generation failure
- ❌ Showing the actual diff per step (US-007)
- ❌ Navigation between steps (US-009)

### 4. File-by-file Fallback

When the user clicks Skip on plan generation failure, build the fallback plan programmatically in Rust — no AI call needed:

```rust
pub fn fallback_review_plan(session: &ReviewSession) -> ReviewPlan {
    let steps = session.changed_files.iter().map(|f| {
        ReviewStep {
            title: format!("Review {}", f.path),
            rationale: format!("{} file", f.status),
            file_refs: vec![FileRef {
                path: f.path.clone(),
                diff_lines: None, // entire file
            }],
        }
    }).collect();

    ReviewPlan {
        steps,
        generated_at: chrono_now_iso(),
    }
}
```

One step per changed file, ordered as git reports them. Simple, predictable, still gives the user a walkthrough structure. Persist this the same way as an AI-generated plan so downstream code (US-007) is agnostic to origin.

Then for a given `FileRef { path, diff_lines: Some((start, end)) }`, take that file's segment and extract lines `start..=end`. For `diff_lines: None`, take the whole segment.

## Why This Approach

- **Flat `FileRef` with optional line ranges** avoids a hunk-indexing layer that would require pre-parsing and sync management — the diff string itself is the source of truth
- **JSON-in-fence prompting** is the most reliable structured output strategy for CLI-based LLMs without function calling support
- **3-tier JSON extraction** is battle-tested and handles markdown wrapping, preamble text, and raw JSON equally
- **New page for guide** gives clean separation for the sidebar layout coming in US-007/US-009 without HTMX layout gymnastics

## Watch Out For

- **Diff truncation at 80k chars** (already in `build_context`) means the AI might reference files/lines that were truncated — validate `FileRef.path` against `changed_files` and silently drop invalid refs
- **AI returning line ranges that don't exist** — clamp to actual segment length in US-007 rather than failing
- **Large diffs producing huge step counts** — consider adding a `max_steps: 15` hint in the prompt to keep plans manageable

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::git_analysis::{self, ChangedFile, GitAnalysis};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct SummaryData {
    pub overview: Option<String>,
    pub changes: Option<String>,
    pub approach: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChatMessage {
    pub role: String,
    pub content: String,
    pub timestamp: String,

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReviewSession {
    pub id: String,
    pub repo_path: String,
    pub branch: String,
    pub default_branch: String,
    pub merge_base: String,
    pub diff: String,
    pub changed_files: Vec<ChangedFile>,
    pub created_at: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub summary: SummaryData,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub chat_messages: Vec<ChatMessage>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub metrics: DiffMetrics,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct DiffMetrics {
    pub files_changed: usize,
    pub lines_added: usize,
    pub lines_removed: usize,
    pub commits_on_branch: usize,
}

impl ReviewSession {
    pub fn new(analysis: GitAnalysis) -> Self {
        let millis = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
            .as_millis();
        let id = format!("review-{millis}");

        let created_at = {
            let secs = millis / 1000;
            let remaining_millis = millis % 1000;
            let days_since_epoch = secs / 86400;
            let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
            let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
            let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
            let seconds = time_of_day % 60;

            let (year, month, day) = days_to_ymd(days_since_epoch as i64);
            format!(
                "{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}.{remaining_millis:03}Z"
            )
        };

        let (lines_added, lines_removed) = git_analysis::compute_diff_line_stats(&analysis.diff);
        let metrics = DiffMetrics {
            files_changed: analysis.changed_files.len(),
            lines_added,
            lines_removed,
            commits_on_branch: analysis.commit_count,
        };

        Self {
            id,
            repo_path: analysis.repo_path,
            branch: analysis.current_branch,
            default_branch: analysis.default_branch,
            merge_base: analysis.merge_base,
            diff: analysis.diff,
            changed_files: analysis.changed_files,
            created_at,
            summary: SummaryData::default(),
            chat_messages: Vec::new(),
            metrics,
        }
    }

    pub fn sessions_dir() -> Result<PathBuf, SessionError> {
        dirs::home_dir()
            .map(|h| h.join(".sherpa").join("sessions"))
            .ok_or(SessionError::NoHomeDir)
    }

    pub fn save(&self) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let dir = Self::sessions_dir()?;
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;

        let file_path = dir.join(format!("{}.json", self.id));
        let content = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(SessionError::Serialize)?;

        let tmp_path = file_path.with_extension("json.tmp");
        let mut file = fs::File::create(&tmp_path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        file.write_all(content.as_bytes())
            .map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        file.sync_all().map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        fs::rename(&tmp_path, &file_path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;

        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn load(id: &str) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
        let dir = Self::sessions_dir()?;
        let file_path = dir.join(format!("{id}.json"));
        Self::load_from(&file_path)
    }

    fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
        if !path.exists() {
            return Err(SessionError::NotFound(path.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
        }
        let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        serde_json::from_str(&content).map_err(SessionError::Parse)
    }
}

fn days_to_ymd(mut days: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    days += 719_468;
    let era = if days >= 0 { days } else { days - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (days - era * 146_097) as u32;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    (year, m, d)
}

#[derive(Debug)]

fn days_to_ymd(mut days: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    days += 719_468;

    pub summary: SummaryData,

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct DiffMetrics {
    pub files_changed: usize,
    pub lines_added: usize,
    pub lines_removed: usize,
    pub commits_on_branch: usize,
}

impl ReviewSession {
    pub fn new(analysis: GitAnalysis) -> Self {
        let millis = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
            .as_millis();
        let id = format!("review-{millis}");

        let created_at = {
            let secs = millis / 1000;
            let remaining_millis = millis % 1000;
            let days_since_epoch = secs / 86400;
            let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
            let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
            let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
            let seconds = time_of_day % 60;

            let (year, month, day) = days_to_ymd(days_since_epoch as i64);
            format!(
                "{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}.{remaining_millis:03}Z"
            )
        };

        let (lines_added, lines_removed) = git_analysis::compute_diff_line_stats(&analysis.diff);
        let metrics = DiffMetrics {
            files_changed: analysis.changed_files.len(),
            lines_added,
            lines_removed,
            commits_on_branch: analysis.commit_count,
        };

        Self {
            id,
            repo_path: analysis.repo_path,
            branch: analysis.current_branch,
            default_branch: analysis.default_branch,
            merge_base: analysis.merge_base,
            diff: analysis.diff,
            changed_files: analysis.changed_files,
            created_at,
            summary: SummaryData::default(),
            chat_messages: Vec::new(),
            metrics,
            review_plan: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn sessions_dir() -> Result<PathBuf, SessionError> {
        dirs::home_dir()
            .map(|h| h.join(".sherpa").join("sessions"))
            .ok_or(SessionError::NoHomeDir)
    }

    pub fn save(&self) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let dir = Self::sessions_dir()?;
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;

        let file_path = dir.join(format!("{}.json", self.id));
        let content = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(SessionError::Serialize)?;

        let tmp_path = file_path.with_extension("json.tmp");
        let mut file = fs::File::create(&tmp_path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        file.write_all(content.as_bytes())
            .map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        file.sync_all().map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        fs::rename(&tmp_path, &file_path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;

        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn load(id: &str) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
        let dir = Self::sessions_dir()?;
        let file_path = dir.join(format!("{id}.json"));
        Self::load_from(&file_path)
    }

    fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
        if !path.exists() {
            return Err(SessionError::NotFound(path.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
        }
        let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(SessionError::Io)?;
        serde_json::from_str(&content).map_err(SessionError::Parse)
    }
}

pub fn fallback_review_plan(session: &ReviewSession) -> ReviewPlan {
    let steps = session
        .changed_files
        .iter()
        .map(|f| ReviewStep {
            title: format!("Review {}", f.path),
            rationale: format!("{} file", f.status),
            file_refs: vec![FileRef {
                path: f.path.clone(),
                diff_lines: None,
            }],
        })
        .collect();

    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
        .as_millis();
    let secs = millis / 1000;
    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;

    ReviewPlan {
        steps,
        generated_at: format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}"),
    }
}

fn days_to_ymd(mut days: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    days += 719_468;
    let era = if days >= 0 { days } else { days - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (days - era * 146_097) as u32;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    (year, m, d)
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum SessionError {
    Io(std::io::Error),
    Serialize(serde_json::Error),
    Parse(serde_json::Error),
    NotFound(String),
    NoHomeDir,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for SessionError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Io(e) => write!(f, "session I/O error: {e}"),
            Self::Serialize(e) => write!(f, "session serialize error: {e}"),
            Self::Parse(e) => write!(f, "session parse error: {e}"),
            Self::NotFound(path) => write!(f, "session not found: {path}"),
            Self::NoHomeDir => write!(f, "could not determine home directory"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for SessionError {}

}

pub fn extract_json_from_response(raw: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(raw).is_ok() {
        return Ok(raw.to_string());
    }

    if let Some(start) = raw.find("```json") {
        let after = &raw[start + 7..];
        if let Some(end) = after.find("```") {
            let candidate = after[..end].trim();
            if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(candidate).is_ok() {
                return Ok(candidate.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    if let (Some(s), Some(e)) = (raw.find('{'), raw.rfind('}')) {
        if s < e {
            let candidate = &raw[s..=e];
            if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(candidate).is_ok() {
                return Ok(candidate.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    Err("Could not extract valid JSON from AI response".to_string())

    "Analyze this diff and create a step-by-step review plan. Group changes by \
     feature, concept, or architectural layer — NOT necessarily one step per file. \
     A single file's changes may appear in multiple steps if they serve different purposes.\n\n\
     Respond with ONLY a JSON object inside a ```json fence, no other text:\n\
     ```json\n\
     {\n\
       \"steps\": [\n\
         {\n\
           \"title\": \"Short descriptive title\",\n\
           \"rationale\": \"Why review these changes together\",\n\
           \"file_refs\": [\n\
             {\"path\": \"src/foo.rs\", \"diff_lines\": [10, 45]},\n\
             {\"path\": \"src/bar.rs\", \"diff_lines\": null}\n\
           ]\n\
         }\n\
       ]\n\
     }\n\
     ```\n\
     Use diff_lines to reference specific line ranges within each file's diff section, \
     or null for the entire file. Order steps in recommended review sequence."
}

pub fn extract_json_from_response(raw: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(raw).is_ok() {
        return Ok(raw.to_string());
    }

    if let Some(start) = raw.find("```json") {
        let after = &raw[start + 7..];
        if let Some(end) = after.find("```") {
            let candidate = after[..end].trim();
            if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(candidate).is_ok() {
                return Ok(candidate.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    if let (Some(s), Some(e)) = (raw.find('{'), raw.rfind('}')) {
        if s < e {
            let candidate = &raw[s..=e];
            if serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(candidate).is_ok() {
                return Ok(candidate.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    Err("Could not extract valid JSON from AI response".to_string())
}

) -> std::result::Result<(String, bool), String> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(session_id)
        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to load session: {e}"))?;

        return Ok((cached.clone(), true));
    }

    let cli = load_selected_cli().ok_or("No AI backend configured")?;

        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(session_id)
        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to reload session: {e}"))?;
    set_cached(&mut session, content.clone());
    let _ = session.save();

    Ok((content, false))
}

async fn summary_chat(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
    Form(form): Form<ChatForm>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    let user_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "user".to_string(),
        content: form.message.clone(),
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(user_msg);

    let cli = load_selected_cli();
    let ai_response = if let Some(cli) = cli {
        let context = build_ai_context(&session);
        let prompt = AiPrompt {
            context,
            instruction: format!(
                "The user asks: {}\n\nRespond helpfully based on the code changes above.",
                form.message
            ),
        };
        match ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt).await {
            Ok(response) => response,
            Err(e) => format!("AI error: {e}"),
        }
    } else {
        "No AI backend configured. Please set up an AI backend first.".to_string()
    };

    let ai_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "assistant".to_string(),
        content: ai_response,
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(ai_msg);
    let _ = session.save();

    let last_two: Vec<_> = session.chat_messages[session.chat_messages.len() - 2..].to_vec();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/_chat_messages.html",
        data!({"messages": last_two}),
    )
}

    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()

    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
    format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}")
}

#[debug_handler]
async fn guide_page(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    let plan = match &session.review_plan {
        Some(plan) => plan.clone(),
        None => {
            return format::render().redirect(&format!("/review/{session_id}/summary"));
        }
    };

    let steps_data: Vec<serde_json::Value> = plan
        .steps
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, step)| {
            let files: Vec<String> = step.file_refs.iter().map(|f| f.path.clone()).collect();
            serde_json::json!({
                "number": i + 1,
                "title": step.title,
                "rationale": step.rationale,
                "file_count": step.file_refs.len(),
                "files": files,
            })
        })
        .collect();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/guide.html",
        data!({
            "session_id": session.id,
            "branch": session.branch,
            "default_branch": session.default_branch,
            "steps": steps_data,
            "total_steps": plan.steps.len(),
        }),

fn chrono_now() -> String {
    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
        .as_millis();
    let secs = millis / 1000;
    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
    format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}")
}

async fn summary_chat(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
    Form(form): Form<ChatForm>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    let user_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "user".to_string(),
        content: form.message.clone(),
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(user_msg);

    let cli = load_selected_cli();
    let ai_response = if let Some(cli) = cli {
        let context = build_ai_context(&session);
        let prompt = AiPrompt {
            context,
            instruction: format!(
                "The user asks: {}\n\nRespond helpfully based on the code changes above.",
                form.message
            ),
        };
        match ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt).await {
            Ok(response) => response,
            Err(e) => format!("AI error: {e}"),
        }
    } else {
        "No AI backend configured. Please set up an AI backend first.".to_string()
    };

    let ai_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "assistant".to_string(),
        content: ai_response,
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(ai_msg);
    let _ = session.save();

    let last_two: Vec<_> = session.chat_messages[session.chat_messages.len() - 2..].to_vec();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/_chat_messages.html",
        data!({"messages": last_two}),
    )
}

async fn generate_section(
    session_id: &str,
    _section: &str,
    instruction: &str,
    get_cached: fn(&ReviewSession) -> &Option<String>,
    set_cached: fn(&mut ReviewSession, String),
) -> std::result::Result<(String, bool), String> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(session_id)
        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to load session: {e}"))?;

    if let Some(cached) = get_cached(&session) {
        return Ok((cached.clone(), true));
    }

    let cli = load_selected_cli().ok_or("No AI backend configured")?;
    let context = build_ai_context(&session);
    let prompt = AiPrompt {
        context,
        instruction: instruction.to_string(),
    };

    let content = ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(session_id)
        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to reload session: {e}"))?;
    set_cached(&mut session, content.clone());
    let _ = session.save();

    Ok((content, false))
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct ChatForm {
    message: String,
}

#[debug_handler]
async fn summary_chat(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
    Form(form): Form<ChatForm>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    let user_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "user".to_string(),
        content: form.message.clone(),
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(user_msg);

    let cli = load_selected_cli();
    let ai_response = if let Some(cli) = cli {
        let context = build_ai_context(&session);
        let prompt = AiPrompt {
            context,
            instruction: format!(
                "The user asks: {}\n\nRespond helpfully based on the code changes above.",
                form.message
            ),
        };
        match ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt).await {
            Ok(response) => response,
            Err(e) => format!("AI error: {e}"),
        }
    } else {
        "No AI backend configured. Please set up an AI backend first.".to_string()
    };

    let ai_msg = ChatMessage {
        role: "assistant".to_string(),
        content: ai_response,
        timestamp: chrono_now(),
    };
    session.chat_messages.push(ai_msg);
    let _ = session.save();

    let last_two: Vec<_> = session.chat_messages[session.chat_messages.len() - 2..].to_vec();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/_chat_messages.html",
        data!({"messages": last_two}),
    )
}

#[debug_handler]
async fn guide_start(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    if let Some(ref plan) = session.review_plan {
        return format::render().redirect(&format!("/review/{session_id}/guide"));
    }

    let cli = match load_selected_cli() {
        Some(cli) => cli,
        None => {
            return format::render().view(
                &v,
                "review/_plan_error.html",
                data!({
                    "error": "No AI backend configured",
                    "session_id": session_id,
                }),
            );
        }
    };

    let context = build_ai_context(&session);
    let prompt = AiPrompt {
        context,
        instruction: ai_cli::review_plan_instruction().to_string(),
    };

    match ai_cli::generate(cli, &prompt).await {
        Ok(raw_response) => {
            match ai_cli::extract_json_from_response(&raw_response)
                .and_then(|json| {
                    serde_json::from_str::<ReviewPlanResponse>(&json)
                        .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to parse review plan JSON: {e}"))
                })
            {
                Ok(plan_response) => {
                    let mut session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
                        tracing::error!("Failed to reload session: {e}");
                        Error::NotFound
                    })?;
                    session.review_plan = Some(ReviewPlan {
                        steps: plan_response.steps,
                        generated_at: chrono_now(),
                    });
                    let _ = session.save();

                    format::render().redirect(&format!("/review/{session_id}/guide"))
                }
                Err(error) => format::render().view(
                    &v,
                    "review/_plan_error.html",
                    data!({
                        "error": error,
                        "session_id": session_id,
                    }),
                ),
            }
        }
        Err(e) => format::render().view(
            &v,
            "review/_plan_error.html",
            data!({
                "error": e.to_string(),
                "session_id": session_id,
            }),
        ),
    }
}

#[debug_handler]
async fn guide_page(
    ViewEngine(v): ViewEngine<TeraView>,
    Path(session_id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Response> {
    let session = ReviewSession::load(&session_id).map_err(|e| {
        tracing::error!("Failed to load session {session_id}: {e}");
        Error::NotFound
    })?;

    let plan = match &session.review_plan {
        Some(plan) => plan.clone(),
        None => {
            return format::render().redirect(&format!("/review/{session_id}/summary"));
        }
    };

    let steps_data: Vec<serde_json::Value> = plan
        .steps
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, step)| {
            let files: Vec<String> = step.file_refs.iter().map(|f| f.path.clone()).collect();
            serde_json::json!({
                "number": i + 1,
                "title": step.title,
                "rationale": step.rationale,
                "file_count": step.file_refs.len(),
                "files": files,
            })
        })
        .collect();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/guide.html",
        data!({
            "session_id": session.id,
            "branch": session.branch,
            "default_branch": session.default_branch,
            "steps": steps_data,
            "total_steps": plan.steps.len(),
        }),
    )
}

fn chrono_now() -> String {
    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
        .as_millis();
    let secs = millis / 1000;
    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
    format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}")
}

pub fn page_routes() -> Routes {
    Routes::new()
        .prefix("/review")
        .add("/{session_id}/summary", get(summary_page))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/overview", get(summary_overview))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/changes", get(summary_changes))

        .add("/{session_id}/guide/start", post(guide_start))
        .add("/{session_id}/guide/plan/skip", post(guide_plan_skip))
        .add("/{session_id}/guide", get(guide_page))
}

            "branch": session.branch,
            "default_branch": session.default_branch,
            "steps": steps_data,
            "total_steps": plan.steps.len(),
        }),
    )
}

fn chrono_now() -> String {
    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
        .as_millis();
    let secs = millis / 1000;
    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
    format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}")
}

            })
        })
        .collect();

    format::render().view(
        &v,
        "review/guide.html",
        data!({
            "session_id": session.id,
            "branch": session.branch,
            "default_branch": session.default_branch,
            "steps": steps_data,
            "total_steps": plan.steps.len(),
        }),
    )
}

fn chrono_now() -> String {
    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("system clock before UNIX epoch")
        .as_millis();
    let secs = millis / 1000;
    let time_of_day = secs % 86400;
    let hours = time_of_day / 3600;
    let minutes = (time_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let seconds = time_of_day % 60;
    format!("{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}")
}

pub fn page_routes() -> Routes {
    Routes::new()
        .prefix("/review")
        .add("/{session_id}/summary", get(summary_page))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/overview", get(summary_overview))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/changes", get(summary_changes))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/approach", get(summary_approach))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/skip/{section}", get(section_skip))
        .add("/{session_id}/summary/chat", post(summary_chat))
        .add("/{session_id}/guide/start", post(guide_start))
        .add("/{session_id}/guide/plan/skip", post(guide_plan_skip))
        .add("/{session_id}/guide", get(guide_page))
}

pub fn api_routes() -> Routes {
    Routes::new().prefix("/api/review")

    fn test_instruction_strings_not_empty() {
        assert!(!overview_instruction().is_empty());
        assert!(!changes_instruction().is_empty());
        assert!(!approach_instruction().is_empty());
        assert!(!review_plan_instruction().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_extract_json_raw_json() {
        let raw = r#"{"steps": [{"title": "t", "rationale": "r", "file_refs": []}]}"#;
        let result = extract_json_from_response(raw).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result, raw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_extract_json_fenced_block() {
        let raw = "Here is the plan:\n```json\n{\"steps\": []}\n```\nDone.";
        let result = extract_json_from_response(raw).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result, "{\"steps\": []}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_extract_json_first_brace_to_last() {
        let raw = "Some preamble text {\"steps\": []} and trailing text";
        let result = extract_json_from_response(raw).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result, "{\"steps\": []}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_extract_json_no_json() {
        let raw = "This has no JSON at all";
        let result = extract_json_from_response(raw);
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_extract_json_invalid_fenced_falls_back() {
        let raw = "```json\nnot valid json\n```\n{\"valid\": true}";
        let result = extract_json_from_response(raw).unwrap();

use tokio::process::Command;

use super::cli_detection::AiCli;

const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 120;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct AiPrompt {
    pub context: String,
    pub instruction: String,
}

impl AiPrompt {
    pub fn full_prompt(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}\n\n{}", self.context, self.instruction)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum AiCliError {
    SpawnFailed(std::io::Error),
    CliFailure { stderr: String },
    Timeout,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for AiCliError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::SpawnFailed(e) => write!(f, "Failed to start AI CLI: {e}"),
            Self::CliFailure { stderr } => write!(f, "AI CLI error: {stderr}"),
            Self::Timeout => write!(f, "AI request timed out"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for AiCliError {}

pub async fn generate(cli: AiCli, prompt: &AiPrompt) -> Result<String, AiCliError> {
